## Left open by the earlier read (RD-072)

An independent reader judged the previous rewrite of this lesson. Fix everything below as well. Each item is as serious as an item under "Fix these".

### Findings

1. Rule B01 (Blocker). Problem: The classification test, judicial warrant procedures, warrant exceptions, and other legal claims have no supplied authoritative source text. B01 source confirmation cannot be completed from the prompt alone; this does not assert that the claims are false.
   > A law may group people for different treatment when there is a sound reason.
2. Rule L18 (Major). Problem: The lesson develops valid consent versus mere submission and hot-pursuit arrest based on personal knowledge as distinct application scenarios. Its examples only work through in-presence arrest and search incident to arrest; neither of these other developed exceptions receives a worked case.
   > Another search exception is freely given, valid consent.
3. Rule L27 (Major). Problem: The same-offense rule depends on unspecified legal conditions. The lesson supplies no reminder, prerequisite reference, or later pointer to valid charge, competent court, plea, and protected termination. Merely saying conditions exist does not explain when this rule applies; the separate law/ordinance rule does not fill that gap.
   > Section $21$ protects against **double jeopardy**, being put at risk of punishment again for the same offense after the legal conditions are met.

### Brief items not fixed

1. Item `lesson-philippine-constitution-bill-of-rights|L18|0`: The examples cover section count, one broad section-range lookup, and debt. They do not work through the other distinct location tasks represented by the catalogue, nor do they give a worked case for recognizing the catalogue's limits, so coverage of the recorded learning goal is incomplete. Reason: A catalogue lesson cannot give an example for every section; three examples are acceptable.
   Reader's note: The rewrite adds several location and application cases, but developed warrant exceptions still lack worked coverage.
